records.title: Causally valid two-candidate authority selection
records.hypothesis: A final decision interface can use a late authority cue to select between two candidate operations when trained end to end.
records.result: All four S4 arms reached 40/40 validation selection, 20/20 counterfactual flips and 20/20 paired correctness, including the unseen layout.
limits: Does not establish arbitrary instruction hierarchy or autonomous reasoning
unresolved: Which internal pathway mediates the final decision
Whether the result transfers to variable candidate counts

records.title: D2 component ablation
records.hypothesis: The S4 improvement is attributable to candidate-slot readout and/or decision-only training rather than the original D2 configuration.
records.result: C1, C2 and C3 all passed; C4 remained below training competence. Operation-class decision-only was sufficient in the two-candidate task, but C4 was historical and not retrained under the crossed-cell trajectory.
limits: C4 is a reused historical checkpoint
Objective and training trajectory are not causally separated
unresolved: Whether the original D2 failure is caused by multi-task loss, its interaction with operation-class readout, or schedule/initialization

records.title: Dynamic shared scoring for compositional authority transfer
records.hypothesis: A shared query/candidate scorer will transfer authority selection from three candidates to four candidates and unseen layouts.
records.result: The gate achieved 72/120 four-candidate pointer accuracy and 0/24 paired counterfactual correctness. Abstention was 24/24; positional transfer was poor and relation matching was partial.
limits: New readout rather than the original S4 head
Does not prove shared scoring impossible
unresolved: Whether explicit candidate identifiers improve cardinality transfer

records.title: Explicit candidate-ID matching across cardinalities
records.hypothesis: Separating candidate-ID extraction from matching will reveal whether shared scoring can transfer across 2/3 to 4/5/8 candidates.
interventions: Matched fixed-slot head versus shared scorer
records.result: The deterministic oracle passed 2064/2064 rows. None of the eight learned arms passed the 95% training gate: fixed-slot arms reached 384--388/576 and shared-scorer arms 444--497/576. Learned transfer is therefore not interpretable.
limits: No learned arm mastered the training task
Does not show that shared scoring is impossible
unresolved: Whether candidate extraction, matching, optimization or task representation caused the learned underfit
Whether a competent shared scorer can transfer across cardinalities
